name: load_mzml_summary
title: Summarise an mzML file
description:
Summarise the first spectra of a local .mzML file as compact text.

For each spectrum reports MS level, retention time, total ion current,
peak count, the ten most intense peaks and the base peak.  Use it to
inspect an acquisition before scoring or searching it.

Output is capped at *max_spectra* spectra to stay inside the context
window; the footer states the file's total spectrum count.

file_path.description: Path to a local .mzML file, absolute or relative to the server working directory.
file_path.title: File Path

max_spectra.description: How many spectra to summarise. Raise it to look further into the run.
max_spectra.title: Max Spectra

noise_threshold.description: Minimum absolute intensity; peaks below this are omitted. 0.0 keeps every peak.
noise_threshold.title: Noise Threshold

name: list_spectra
title: List spectra in an MS file
description:
List the spectra in a local MS file as a compact index table.

Reads .mzML, .mzML.gz, .mgf and .imzML (imaging) files; the reader is
chosen from the file extension.  For each spectrum reports its index,
MS level, retention time, precursor m/z and peak count, so you can
choose which spectrum to hand to `load_spectrum` or search.

Use it before `load_spectrum`: an MS/MS library search needs an MS2
query, and a real LC-MS run interleaves MS1 survey scans with the MS2
spectra worth searching.  Filter with `ms_level=2` and `min_peaks` to
see the candidates without reading every spectrum's peaks.

The scan stops as soon as `max_spectra` matches are collected, and it
never reads more than the server's per-request spectrum budget
(`MSMCP_MAX_SPECTRA`); the footer says which ceiling stopped it, so a
truncated listing never looks like a complete one.  It is slower than
`load_mzml_summary` on large runs but far cheaper than loading every
spectrum, and spectra the filter excludes are still counted.

file_path.description: Path to a local MS file (.mzML, .mzML.gz, .mgf or .imzML), absolute or relative to the server working directory.
file_path.title: File Path

ms_level.description: Only list spectra at this MS level (for example 2 for MS/MS). Leave unset to list every level.
ms_level.title: Ms Level

max_spectra.description: Maximum number of spectra to list; the scan stops once this many match.
max_spectra.title: Max Spectra

min_peaks.description: Only list spectra with at least this many peaks. 0 lists spectra with no peaks too.
min_peaks.title: Min Peaks

name: load_spectrum
title: Load a spectrum as a server-side reference
description:
Load one spectrum server-side and return its data reference.

The peaks stay on the server: this returns a short ``ptr:spectrum:...``
reference plus metadata and provenance, never the peak arrays.  Pass the
reference to other tools (for example `compute_cosine` or
`search_library`) so a large spectrum never has to be copied through the
conversation.

Use `summarise_reference` to read the spectrum's contents and
`release_reference` when you are done with it.  References expire
automatically after a retention period.

file_path.description: Path to a local .mzML, .mzML.gz, .mgf or .imzML file. The reader is chosen from the file extension.
file_path.title: File Path

spectrum_index.description: Zero-based index of the spectrum to load. The index must be below the configured per-request spectrum limit.
spectrum_index.title: Spectrum Index

output_schema.description:
Structured result of ``load_spectrum``.

Describes the registered spectrum in full without containing it: the peaks
stay on the server behind ``reference``.

kind.description: Data kind held by the reference.
kind.title: Kind

source.description: Path the spectrum was read from.
source.title: Source

spectrum_index.description: Index of the spectrum within the source.
spectrum_index.title: Spectrum Index

ms_level.description: MS level, when the source states it.
ms_level.title: Ms Level

coordinate.description: (x, y, z) pixel for imaging sources; null otherwise.
coordinate.title: Coordinate

tic.description: Total ion current (sum of all intensities).
tic.title: Tic

n_bytes.description: Size of the stored peak arrays.
n_bytes.title: N Bytes

provenance.description: Structured provenance for this derived object.
provenance.title: Provenance

output_schema.title: SpectrumReferenceResult

name: summarise_reference
title: Summarise a referenced spectrum
description:
Summarise a spectrum held behind a data reference.

Reads the peaks from server memory: the source file is not opened
again, and nothing large is transferred.  Use it to inspect data you
have already loaded with `load_spectrum`.

Reports the same compact per-spectrum block as `load_mzml_summary`,
followed by the provenance of the referenced object.

reference.description: A data reference returned by load_spectrum, e.g. 'ptr:spectrum:1a2b...'.
reference.title: Reference

name: release_reference
title: Release a data reference
description:
Release a server-side data reference you no longer need.

Frees the stored peaks immediately instead of waiting for the retention
period to expire.  Releasing is idempotent: releasing an already-released
or unknown reference reports that it was already gone rather than
failing, so a retry after a lost response is always safe.

reference.description: A data reference returned by load_spectrum, e.g. 'ptr:spectrum:1a2b...'.
reference.title: Reference

name: extract_chromatograms
title: Extract scan-level chromatograms
description:
Return structured TIC, BPC and optional XIC traces from one bounded pass.

TIC is the sum of reported intensities per selected scan. BPC is its
maximum reported intensity, or null for an empty scan. Each XIC sums
all reported points in the inclusive m/z window. Each returned point
carries the scan's stated polarity, or null when unavailable.
Representation is
reported when the acquisition states centroid or profile; unknown
representation remains unknown and is called out in warnings. No
smoothing, normalization, alignment, baseline correction, blank
subtraction, or identification is performed. The tool scans the full
source to report acquisition counts and coverage; the optional RT range
filters returned trace points only.

file_path.description: Path to a local .mzML or .mzML.gz acquisition inside the configured allowed root.
file_path.title: File Path

targets_mz.description: Finite positive target m/z values for simultaneous XICs; up to 20. Use an empty list or null for TIC and BPC only.
targets_mz.title: Targets Mz

tolerance.description: Half-width of each XIC window, in the selected tolerance_unit.
tolerance.title: Tolerance

tolerance_unit.description: Tolerance units: ppm relative to target m/z, or absolute Da.
tolerance_unit.title: Tolerance Unit

ms_level.description: MS level included in the chromatogram traces; defaults to MS1.
ms_level.title: Ms Level

retention_time_range_min.description: Optional inclusive [start, end] retention-time range in minutes.
retention_time_range_min.title: Retention Time Range Min

max_spectra.description: Maximum source spectra to scan, across all MS levels and retention times; hard maximum 10000.
max_spectra.title: Max Spectra

name: predict_adduct_offset
title: Predict Adduct Mass Offset
description:
Return the exact mass shift that a standard ionisation adduct adds to a neutral molecule.

Use this to convert a neutral monoisotopic mass into the expected
precursor m/z for a given ionisation pathway, or to check whether an
adduct assignment is physically plausible.

Returns the adduct polarity, charge state, exact mass shift in daltons
(Da), and the formula for the resulting m/z offset.  Note that for a
charge state of 1 the reported shift is the direct m/z offset, whereas
for higher charge states the shift must be divided by the absolute
charge (the returned offset formula already shows this).

Only canonical adduct notations from a fixed table are accepted (e.g.
'[M+H]+', '[M+Na]+', '[M+NH4]+', '[M+H-H2O]+', '[M+2H]2+', '[M-H]-',
'[M+Cl]-', '[M+HCOO]-'); matching is case-insensitive.  Any other
string is rejected and the supported adducts are listed, so do not
invent an adduct that is not offered there.  The adduct string must be
at least 3 characters long.

adduct_string.description: Adduct notation, e.g. '[M+H]+', '[M-H]-' or '[M+Na]+'. Must be one of the instrument-standard adducts.
adduct_string.title: Adduct String

name: annotate_isotopes
title: Annotate Isotope Pattern
description:
Predict the theoretical isotope pattern (M, M+1, ...) of a compound.

Use this to obtain isotopologue masses and relative abundances, for
example to check a measured isotope envelope against a proposed
molecular formula or to confirm a monoisotopic mass.

Returns the monoisotopic mass in daltons (Da) and a Markdown table
giving the theoretical mass and relative abundance of each isotopologue
from M up to M+(isotopologues-1), normalised so that the monoisotopic
peak is 1.0000.  The envelope is the exact multinomial expansion of each
element's isotopes, so it handles the full isotope ladder: a chlorine-
or bromine-rich formula carries its signal in M+2 and M+4 (Cl and Br
have no single-neutron isotope), while ordinary C/H/N/O compounds
concentrate it in M+1 and M+2.  Raise `isotopologues` to reveal the
higher peaks a halogen-rich formula carries.

Pass a chemical formula as the identifier by default (for example
'C6H12O6'); set is_smiles=True only when the identifier is a SMILES
string.  SMILES resolution requires the optional RDKit dependency: if
it is missing, an error is returned and the formula should be supplied
instead.  The identifier must be at least one character long, and only
elements with tabulated isotope data are supported (C, H, N, O, S, P,
F, Cl, Br, I, Na, K, Si, Fe, Se) - any other element returns an error.
Formulae are limited to 10,000 total atoms so the exact expansion remains
bounded for the small-molecule use case.

identifier.description: Chemical formula (e.g. 'C6H12O6') or SMILES string, depending on is_smiles; maximum 4096 characters.
identifier.title: Identifier

is_smiles.description: Set to True when identifier is a SMILES string; leave False when it is a chemical formula.
is_smiles.title: Is Smiles

isotopologues.description: How many isotopologue rows to return, from M up to M+(isotopologues-1). Default 3 (M, M+1, M+2). Raise it for halogen-rich formulas, whose diagnostic M+4 peak needs more rows.
isotopologues.title: Isotopologues

name: validate_precursor
title: Validate Precursor Mass
description:
Check whether an observed precursor mass matches a theoretical mass.

Use this before interpreting an MS/MS spectrum to confirm that the
precursor ion is physically consistent with the hypothesised compound,
or to discriminate between candidate molecular formulas, adducts or
charge states.

Both masses must be given in daltons (Da) and must be greater than 0;
the theoretical mass is the exact monoisotopic mass of the neutral (or
already ionised) species being compared, and the experimental mass is
the observed precursor m/z.

Returns the mass error together with a PASSED or REJECTED verdict.  The
acceptance window is not a fixed number: it comes from the instrument
class named by `instrument_class` (default 'generic', the 5.0 ppm gate
MSMCP has used since v1.0).  Accurate-mass classes express the window in
ppm; unit-resolution classes (ion_trap, triple_quad) use a dalton
window, because a ppm gate is meaningless on an instrument that cannot
resolve fractions of a nominal mass.  The class and the window actually
applied are stated in the result, so a verdict is never separated from
the assumption behind it.  A rejection means the observation is
inconsistent with the hypothesis under that assumption, and the formula,
adduct assignment or instrument calibration should be reconsidered.

theoretical_mass.description: Finite, positive exact monoisotopic mass of the hypothesised compound (Da).
theoretical_mass.title: Theoretical Mass

experimental_mass.description: Finite, positive experimentally observed precursor m/z (Da).
experimental_mass.title: Experimental Mass

instrument_class.description: Instrument class whose documented default precursor tolerance is applied (default 'generic' — MSMCP's v1.0 5.0 ppm gate).  Accurate-mass classes tolerate ppm; unit-resolution classes (ion_trap, triple_quad) use a Da window.  One of: generic, ion_trap, orbitrap, tof, triple_quad.
instrument_class.title: Instrument Class

name: compute_cosine
title: Compute MS/MS Cosine Similarity
description:
Score the similarity between an experimental MS/MS spectrum and a reference spectrum.

Use this for spectral library matching, to rank candidate reference
spectra against an unknown query spectrum, or to judge how well a
proposed structure explains the observed fragmentation.

Each side comes from exactly one source.  Either pass peaks directly as
[[m/z, intensity], ...] lists in daltons — each list needs at least one
peak, intensities must be non-negative, and intensities should be on a
consistent scale within each spectrum — or pass a `query_reference` /
`reference_reference` naming data already loaded server-side, which
keeps a large spectrum out of the conversation.  Supplying both sources
for the same side, or neither, is rejected.

Returns a cosine score between 0 and 1, the number of matched peaks and
the percentage of query peaks matched, and a list of the most intense
unmatched query peaks, which point at structural differences to
investigate.  The score is the dot product of the matched peak
intensities normalised over **all** peaks in each spectrum, so 1.0 means
the matched peaks account for all of the intensity in both spectra —
not that the two spectra are identical; a spectrum that shares a single
peak with the query scores near zero, not 1.0.  The response names the
source of each side, so a score is traceable back to where its peaks
came from.

With scoring_method='classical' (the default) query peaks are matched
to the closest unused reference peak within ms2_tolerance Da (greedy,
one-to-one), so the tolerance must be greater than 0 and at most 1.0.
When ms2_tolerance is left unset it is the documented default for the
named `instrument_class` (0.02 Da for 'generic'); the response states
the window applied and where it came from.
With 'dreams' or 'lsm-ms2' the comparison happens in whole-spectrum
embedding space instead and no peak-matching counts are reported;
those methods need the corresponding foundation model to be installed,
otherwise the tool returns an error rather than a score.

query_peaks.description: Query spectrum peaks as [[m/z, intensity], ...]; m/z must be finite and positive, and intensity finite and non-negative. Provide this or query_reference, not both.
query_peaks.title: Query Peaks

query_reference.description: A reference from load_spectrum (or a stored peak list), used as the query instead of inline peaks.  Provide this or query_peaks, not both.
query_reference.title: Query Reference

reference_peaks.description: Reference spectrum peaks as [[m/z, intensity], ...]; m/z must be finite and positive, and intensity finite and non-negative. Provide this or reference_reference, not both.
reference_peaks.title: Reference Peaks

reference_reference.description: A reference from load_spectrum (or a stored peak list), used as the reference spectrum instead of inline peaks.  Provide this or reference_peaks, not both.
reference_reference.title: Reference Reference

ms2_tolerance.description: m/z matching tolerance in Da; must be greater than 0 and at most 1.0.  Leave unset to use the default for the instrument class (0.02 Da for 'generic').
ms2_tolerance.title: Ms2 Tolerance

instrument_class.description: Instrument class whose documented default m/z window is used when ms2_tolerance is not given (default 'generic').  One of: generic, ion_trap, orbitrap, tof, triple_quad.
instrument_class.title: Instrument Class

scoring_method.description: Scoring method: 'classical' performs greedy one-to-one peak matching within ms2_tolerance, while 'dreams' and 'lsm-ms2' compare whole-spectrum embeddings from the corresponding foundation model.
scoring_method.title: Scoring Method

name: search_library
title: Search a spectral library (async)
description:
Start a background spectral-library search and return a job ID.

The **library** is read for real when `database_file` names a format
MSMCP can read (MSP/NIST-style text and MGF, `.msp` / `.msp.gz` / `.mgf` / `.mgf.gz`).  The path is
resolved through the same security boundary as acquisitions — allowed
root, size limit, read-only — so a library outside the allowed root, a
missing file or an unsupported format is refused before a job is
dispatched.  A path with no reader falls back to a deterministic
synthetic library, and the report says which path was used; never treat
a synthetic-library hit as a compound identification.

The **query** spectrum can be real: pass `spectrum_reference` from
`load_spectrum` (peaks already server-side), or `experimental_file` with
`spectrum_index` to read one from disk.  The reply names the spectrum it
used — index, MS level, retention time, precursor m/z and peak count —
because the first spectrum of a real LC/MS run is normally an MS1 survey
scan.  An MS1 (or non-MS2) query is refused: it is not evidence for an
MS2 library match.  A spectrum with no peaks is refused rather than
dispatched.  The chunked scan and similarity ranking use the selected
library in every case.

When the query is MS2 and states a precursor m/z, the declared
instrument-class precursor tolerance is applied before ranking;
candidates whose stated polarity, charge or adduct conflicts with the
query are also excluded.  Candidates that omit a field remain ranked but
are labelled *unknown*, and a direct peak-list query (no acquisition
context) is reported as fragment-only exploratory.  The report and
provenance record the eligibility counts, exclusion reasons and only the
tolerances actually applied.  Significance is uncalibrated; no
statistical error-rate claim is made.

The MS2 m/z matching window comes from the named `instrument_class`
(default 'generic'). The class and matching window are stated in the
report and recorded in provenance. No significance threshold is applied,
and ranked scores are not identification probabilities or error rates.
Scoring requires finite positive m/z coordinates and finite
non-negative intensities; non-positive coordinates and signed
baseline-corrected peaks are rejected, not clipped or scored as cosine
similarity.

Returns immediately with a job ID, because the scan takes far longer
than a request timeout.  Poll `check_search_status` with that ID to
collect the report.  This tool does not return results directly.

database_file.description: Path to the spectral library.  MSP/NIST-style text (.msp, .msp.gz) and MGF (.mgf, .mgf.gz) are read from disk through the security boundary; any other path falls back to a labelled synthetic library.
database_file.title: Database File

experimental_file.description: Path to the experimental spectrum file, read for real through the ingestion layer.  Provide this or spectrum_reference, not both.
experimental_file.title: Experimental File

spectrum_index.description: Zero-based index of the spectrum to search inside experimental_file (default 0).  A real LC-MS/MS file starts with an MS1 survey scan, so check which spectrum you want with load_mzml_summary or load_spectrum first — the reply always names the spectrum that was used.
spectrum_index.title: Spectrum Index

spectrum_reference.description: A spectrum reference from load_spectrum, used as the query instead of a file path.  Provide this or experimental_file, not both.
spectrum_reference.title: Spectrum Reference

scoring_method.description: 'classical' is greedy peak matching; 'dreams' and 'lsm-ms2' are real foundation-model embeddings, which need the optional ML backend installed or the job fails.
scoring_method.title: Scoring Method

chunk_size.description: Spectra read per database batch.  Affects only memory and I/O batching, not the result.
chunk_size.title: Chunk Size

instrument_class.description: Instrument class whose documented defaults set the experimental thresholds this scan applies — the MS2 m/z window (default 'generic').  The class and the values used are recorded in the report and its provenance.  One of: generic, ion_trap, orbitrap, tof, triple_quad.
instrument_class.title: Instrument Class

name: check_search_status
title: Check search status
description:
Fetch the current state, or the report, of a background search.

Pass the job ID returned by `search_library`.  While the job is queued
or scanning this returns a short status line, so poll again after a
pause.

The finished report is delivered **once**: the first poll after the job
completes returns the full Markdown report, and any later poll returns
a short digest of it (library size, hit count, top hit) so that a client
which keeps polling does not pull the whole report into its context
again.  Pass `full_report=True` to get the report itself back when it is
no longer in context.  A failed or cancelled job is reported as such on
every poll.

A job the server no longer knows about (for example after a restart)
is reported as failed rather than as pending, so it is always safe to
keep polling.

job_id.description: The job ID returned by search_library.
job_id.title: Job Id

full_report.description: Request the whole report again after it has already been returned once.  Leave it false to keep repeat polls small.
full_report.title: Full Report

name: cancel_search
title: Cancel a search
description:
Abort a queued or running background search.

Pass the job ID returned by `search_library`.  A job that has already
finished is reported as such rather than cancelled.  A scan that has
already started may not stop instantly, but its partial work is
discarded instead of being returned.

Poll `check_search_status` afterwards to confirm the job reached the
cancelled state.

job_id.description: The job ID returned by search_library.
job_id.title: Job Id

name: generate_qc_summary
title: Generate a QC summary
description:
Report quality-control metrics for a local MS acquisition.

Reads .mzML, .mzML.gz, .mgf and .imzML (imaging) files; the reader is
chosen from the file extension. Scans at most the configured per-request
spectrum limit and reports when full-acquisition coverage is unconfirmed.
Metrics include total-ion-current counts, per-spectrum peak density, an
*estimated* signal-to-noise ratio (base peak / median positive
intensity, a transparent proxy rather than a calibrated instrument
SNR), and the prevalence of ten diagnostic immonium and oxonium
fragment ions.

The two experimental thresholds — the diagnostic-ion matching window
and the SNR bands used for the low/high prevalence rows — come from the
named `instrument_class` (default 'generic': +/-0.02 Da and 5/20 SNR,
MSMCP's v1.0 values), and the values actually applied are stated in the
report, so a QC verdict is never separated from the assumption behind
it.

Use it to judge whether an acquisition is worth searching. Unlike
`load_mzml_summary`, it may scan up to the configured spectrum limit;
it never presents a capped summary as covering the full acquisition.

file_path.description: Path to a local MS file (.mzML, .mzML.gz, .mgf or .imzML), absolute or relative to the server working directory.
file_path.title: File Path

instrument_class.description: Instrument class whose documented defaults set the diagnostic-ion matching window and the SNR reporting bands (default 'generic': ±0.02 Da, 5/20 SNR).  One of: generic, ion_trap, orbitrap, tof, triple_quad.
instrument_class.title: Instrument Class

name: ping
title: Server health check
description:
Check that the core server is running.

Takes no arguments. The optional `massflow` distribution is reported
from installed metadata without importing it; absence is normal for
core mzML/MGF installs. These fields do not verify imzML compatibility
or the separate analytical MassFlow engine. Backend import failures
are reported when reading imzML, with imaging-extra install guidance.

output_schema.description: Response schema for the diagnostic ping tool.

massflow_available.description: True when `massflow` distribution metadata is installed; does not verify the optional imzML backend or analytical MassFlow engine.
massflow_available.title: Massflow Available

massflow_version.description: Installed `massflow` distribution version, or null when absent.
massflow_version.title: Massflow Version

output_schema.title: PingResponse
